requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 486 AND state = 'new' AND reopen_count = 1 AND channel = 'email'
assumptions: the case is 486 (CS-0000486): the only closed case of Larson PLC (account 22) on Apache HTTP Server Variant 70 (product 90), matching 'the outage we thought was fixed'
reopened state is new: the policy's lifecycle names new as the state a resolved case returns to; closed to new is not listed, but the request asks to reopen
reopen_count goes from its seed value 0 to 1 on this one reopening
channel email kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the seed holds alert; the follow-up arrived by mail, but the request does not ask for the channel to change)

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 486 AND contact_id = 38
assumptions: Denise Hawkins is user 7, whose contact record at Larson PLC is contact 38
a case holds one contact_id, so including her means setting it to 38 in place of contact 40

requirements.text: assign it to Christine Evans in CSM Tier 1 Support

Christine Evans is user 123, an active agent and a member of group 1, so the policy's assignment constraints hold

requirements.text: that Apache HTTP Server Variant 70 outage at Larson PLC we thought was fixed
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE account_id = 22 AND product_id = 90 AND case_id <> 486 AND reopen_count = 0 AND state <> 'new' AND assigned_to IS NOT 123
assumptions: boundary of the description: cases 479 (in progress), 481 (pending, Denise Hawkins as contact) and 489 (canceled) are Larson PLC cases on the same product; none is the closed outage, so none may be reopened or assigned to Christine Evans in place of 486

disagreement: cells: one pass tests state, reopen_count and assigned_to IS NOT 123, the other state and reopen_count only; chose the tighter form with assigned_to because none of the three cases is assigned to user 123 on the seed and assigning one of them to Christine Evans is the same misreading as reopening it

notes:
The benchmark's reopening check tests state, reopen_count, channel and contact together; it is carried jointly by the reopen and contact requirements, since the request asks for them separately. The policy lists no transition out of closed (only resolved to closed or new); the request asks for the closed case to be reopened, and state new is taken as the reopened state, as the benchmark also expects. closed_on is a server-kept timestamp and is not tested after the reopening. The acting user, Tabitha Bullock, is an agent who is neither assigned to the case nor in its group, but the policy has the assistant act with admin responsibilities by default, so the request is in scope.
disagreement: value: one pass's boundary stay on the other Larson PLC cases of this product also requires assigned_to IS NOT 123, the other's does not; kept the tighter form because it holds on the seed (count 3) and guards against assigning a neighbouring case to Christine Evans in place of 486.
